acceptance_criteria: Dispatch gate (W5, post-O8): no dispatch until O8 is an ancestor of origin/main, re-observed by git ancestry at prereq-check time. O8 is the commit the D1 coordinator records as O8 in its O8 receipt (plan, goal, PR, merge commit): under D5-20261006 the merge commit of the S-08 successor goal, today ACH-S-08 of plan ach-skills-s08-gate-workspace-repair, so a renamed or republished successor carries O8 through that record. Prereq-check confirms the recorded commit is the merge commit of a merged PR on that goal's exact goal branch, and the evidence cites the receipt by path and sha256. The original ACH-S-08 of ach-skills-gate-workspace (generation 22d460b2...) is held, immutable and uncredited: it is never O8, and its preserved claims are not blocking claims for the cross-plan rule. ACH-S-06 (#108), ACH-S-07 (#117) and ACH-GW-DISC-01 (#123) are merged and are not O8. Cross-plan rule: a path that an active goal of another plan claims is edited only after that goal's merge commit reaches origin/main; held, uncredited goals are exempt. The machinery does not enforce cross-plan overlap for goal PRs, so the goal's reviewer checks this rule. Dispatch also waits until the goal PR of TSWC's tswc-sk-b2 (plan tswc-skills-lane, registered by #107) has merged: B2 claims .ai/ci/local-ci.json (the migrate test's sources hash only), tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py, tests/catalog_contract_test.sh and the two retained-policy tests, and B2 states that e6-sk-00-ledger waits for it, so B2 is a one-way prerequisite (E6 yields), not a cross-plan claim conflict; it lapses only if the TSWC coordinator records B2 as withdrawn or B2's plan entry is retired. No waiver exists.

Tool prerequisite and approval timing (D4): dispatch also waits until a separately published policy-amendment generation adds node and npm to the live readiness policy tools[] and merges after O8, so the tooling gate checks them. This live-mode generation scopes no policy file. The amendment is agent-self approvable only while agent-self stays in the candidate's own approval.accept (rule d), emits agent_self_policy_change, flips tests/readiness_policy_v2_test.sh lines 25 and 51-53 and tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py lines 425-426 (precedents #111 and the P5 republish 4fee2ef), and voids every plan approval in the repository, P5's included. This generation keeps its identity. Its plan approval is minted only after O8 and the amendment have merged, immediately before this goal's admission, and is re-signed before certification when fewer than 7 days of the 14-day window remain, because merge-v2 re-verifies it at merge time.

TSWC A5, owned here (D9): ts-tooling/ holds a strict-TypeScript package with devDependencies only, zero runtime dependencies, a committed lockfile installed with npm ci --ignore-scripts by the pinned bootstrap ts-tooling/bootstrap.sh, and no path that enters a catalog payload. tsconfig is the pinned preset: target and lib ES2023, module and moduleResolution NodeNext, strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, forceConsistentCasingInFileNames, verbatimModuleSyntax, skipLibCheck, declaration and sourceMap, with incremental off and no tsBuildInfoFile. Sources are .mts and compile to .mjs. TS test sources live in ts-tooling/test and compile through a separate tsconfig.test.json into ts-tooling/build, which is gitignored, never committed or shipped, and removed by the wrapper on exit.

Strict TS stack (D5): tsc --noEmit under that preset; eslint with typescript-eslint recommendedTypeChecked, complexity 10 (labeled project decision), sonarjs/cognitive-complexity 15 (documented default) and @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises error, run with --max-warnings 0 and without --cache; no eslint-disable, @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck in converted code. A sample entrypoint passes every check, each rule has a violating negative fixture that fails, and a test pins the preset flags and thresholds so relaxing any of them is red.

Callable verification and hygiene: tests/ts_tooling_test.sh runs the toolchain presence and node version checks, tsc --noEmit, eslint, the build, the committed-output drift check, the TS tests and the negative fixtures, prints Results: PASS=n with n > 0, and is reached by bash tests/run-tests.sh. A missing node, npm or devDependency, or a node outside the ADR-0018 range, is red, never skipped. After the checks of tests/ts_tooling_test.sh or tests/legacy_freeze_test.sh run, the untracked and ignored paths (git status --porcelain --ignored) equal those before the run plus only the declared outputs ts-tooling/node_modules and ts-tooling/build; a seeded cache-writing run (for example ruff without --no-cache) is red. Neither wrapper is listed in verification because the publisher refuses a script absent at the base (verification_not_at_base); that check is never relaxed.

TSWC A4, owned here (D6, D9): .ai/rules/legacy-freeze-baseline.json inventories, at this goal's base, every tracked .py file, every non-test .sh file and every test shell that embeds a Python program, in exactly the classes eligible (with its owning goal id, e6-sk-01-py-leaf through e6-sk-05-test-harness, never a placeholder), compat-shim, scaffold-template, test-wrapper and kept-language. kept-language holds the files consumers copy or run outside a skills checkout, each entry citing its consumer: scripts/matrix-contract.py and scripts/render-ci-adapters.py (copied standalone by ai-catapult scripts/build-claude-plugin.sh:85-96 and scripts/build-codex-plugin.sh:88-99, staged by scripts/stage-matrix-runtime.sh and scripts/stage-ci-adapters-runtime.sh, and resolved by src/matrix-runtime.js:11-12), scripts/release/strategy-selector.sh (run from consumers' release templates) and tests/helpers/lock_contention.py, which loads the first two as modules; a kept-language file leaves its class only through a generation that co-plans the consumer change. In-flight legacy files that the 2026-10-07 decision lets open PRs merge as-is (#105 and #118 at publication) are listed with their owning goal and in_flight set to the PR, present or not; tests/local_ci_declaration_test.py from #105 is owned by e6-sk-05-test-harness. This goal never waits for #105, and #105 never fails the ratchet. The C901, xenon, mypy, shellcheck and shfmt baseline is measured at this base; the historical sixteen C901 violations up to complexity 38 are not a measurement.

Ratchet: scripts/check-legacy-freeze.sh (a shim over the TS checker from day one, compiled into scripts/lib) and tests/legacy_freeze_test.sh make the eligible set shrink-only. Growth, a re-added or reclassified entry, an unlisted file, a class change outside this plan, a kept-language file leaving its class, and a present in-flight file whose class differs from its entry are red, each with a negative fixture under tests/fixtures/e6-sk-00-ledger; an absent in-flight entry is green.

Legacy strict stack (D5) over every not-yet-converted and surviving file, run by tests/legacy_freeze_test.sh: ruff check --no-cache with C901 maximum 10, xenon --max-absolute B --max-average A, mypy --strict --cache-dir=/dev/null for new or changed Python with the ledger baseline ratchet, shellcheck -S error, shfmt -d and bash -n, with Python bytecode writing off; no lizard shell CCN gate. The global excludes (tests/fixtures/**, test/fixtures/**, vendor/**, dist/**, dist-snapshot/**, reference/golden-*/**, node_modules/**, .venv/**, site-packages/**) resolve per repository and are pinned by a test. No file is refactored merely to pass. Tool provenance is recorded: brew install shellcheck shfmt; uv tool install ruff, uv tool install mypy and uv tool install xenon, one package per invocation; never brew install lizard. prek registration is e6-sk-01-py-leaf's, so this goal leaves prek.toml and ci-prek.yml untouched.

Registration: .github/workflows/ci.yml's Test Suite job installs the pinned node version and the legacy tools and runs npm ci --ignore-scripts in ts-tooling before tests/run-tests.sh, keeping the job name Test Suite byte-identical; ci-prek.yml and security.yml are unchanged (e6-sk-01-py-leaf edits them when it registers prek hooks and turns the secret scan into a shim). .ai/ci/local-ci.json re-pins ci.yml, pins every new source this goal adds, and declares, through the workspace contract O8 delivers (local-ci/2 at publication), the bootstrap bash ts-tooling/bootstrap.sh with the lockfile pinned and install scripts disabled, the dependency directory ts-tooling/node_modules and the output ts-tooling/build; its verification list is unchanged. ts-tooling/.gitignore ignores both. Nothing under them is syntax-checked or linted as repository code: tests/test-scripts.sh gains only that exclusion, with a test.

Runner and packaging (D4): docs/architecture/adr/0018-ts-tooling-runner-and-packaging.md records one runner (node executing tsc-compiled ESM emitted as .mjs; no type stripping, ts-node, bundler or second runner); one supported node major range, pinned with ts-tooling/package.json engines.node and the workflow's node version, checked by a test, and enforced by a version guard that each compiled entrypoint imports first (node_version_unsupported); compiled modules that import only node: builtins and relative paths; compiled JavaScript committed inside the shipping directory each goal scopes, so installed payloads run with node alone, with a drift check against a fresh build; dependency manifests that pin the executed files; node and npm as required tools; the shim's fixed node flags and the python3 shim's interpreter flags; the TS test output directory; one test-seam mechanism for every later port of a monkeypatching Python test (tests/helpers/lock_contention.py style), either an exported dependency seam or a node:module register() loader hook, chosen once and demonstrated by the sample entrypoint; and the provenance principle that a TS driver replaces a Python driver only after the spec's D13 procedure passes in that PR, with a rollback certified by a source-lane driver pinned to the pre-switch commit. It does not amend ADR-0016.

Shim template (D3): one template per extension, bash for .sh and python3 for .py. A shim clears its environment to an allowlist with env -i semantics (the base names PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL and TMPDIR plus only the names its ledger entry declares, never a NODE_* name), locates the compiled .mjs entrypoint beside itself, resolves node on the allowlisted PATH, and execs node with the fixed flag set ADR-0018 records and unchanged arguments and stdin; without node it fails closed with node_unavailable. node_unavailable and node_version_unsupported print their code on stderr and exit with dedicated statuses distinct from every converted tool's exit codes, so a test can tell them from a tool refusal. tests/e6_shim_conformance_test.sh renders every shim from the template, its entrypoint and its declared names, compares byte-for-byte, checks the exec bit, and fails on a NODE_* allowlist entry. scripts/check-legacy-freeze.sh is the first conforming shim.

Node isolation (G3): tests/e6_node_shadowing_test.sh runs a sample entrypoint through each shim template from a hostile cwd and shows exit status, stdout and stderr byte-identical to a clean run under each probe: NODE_OPTIONS preloading a module (--require and --import), NODE_DEBUG set, a typeless ancestor package.json, an ancestor package.json with type commonjs, node_modules in the cwd shadowing a module name, and, for the python3 shim, PYTHONPATH carrying a sitecustomize. Each probe has a red leg showing that it changes the outcome of an unprotected run (node started directly, or a .js build). A stub node that reports a version outside the ADR-0018 range is refused with node_version_unsupported.

Differential harness (D8): tests/e6_differential_test.sh materializes the reference from git objects by a commit-and-path anchor, checked against its recorded blob id and sha256, never from the working tree; runs it and the candidate on one corpus; and compares exit status, stdout, stderr and written files byte-for-byte. A corpus may declare named normalization classes (name, sites, mask); none applies unless declared, and the spec's interpreter-diagnostic class for v1 is expressible as one. Red legs: a seeded one-byte divergence, an anchor whose blob id or sha256 does not match, an undeclared mask, a mask that would change a byte outside its declared sites, and a candidate run that ends in node_unavailable or node_version_unsupported, which is never a pass.

TDD evidence in .ai/evidence/e6-sk-00-ledger.json records an observed red then green for the same commands, one pair per new check; bash tests/run-tests.sh, prek run --all-files and git diff --check pass at the PR head. No coverage percentage is invented.
